question: Air brakes are actually made up of how many different braking systems?
choice_c: Four: service, parking, emergency and auxiliary
explanation: The manual states air brakes are really three different braking systems: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.M, Air Brake System Overview

question: At approximately what pressure does the governor stop the air compressor from pumping air (the "cut-out" level)?
explanation: When air tank pressure rises to the cut-out level, around 125 psi, the governor stops the compressor from pumping air.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.2, Air Compressor Governor

question: At approximately what pressure does the governor allow the compressor to start pumping air again (the "cut-in" level)?
explanation: When tank pressure falls to the cut-in pressure, around 100 psi, the governor allows the compressor to start pumping again.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.2, Air Compressor Governor

question: Why is it important to drain water and oil from the air tanks?
choice_a: Because water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure
choice_d: Because it is required only in the summer
explanation: Water and oil collect in the bottom of the tank; the water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure, so tanks must be drained completely.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.4, Air Tank Drains

question: A manually operated air tank drain valve must be drained by the driver how often?
choice_b: At the end of each day of driving
choice_c: Only when the low air pressure warning comes on
choice_d: Every time the vehicle is fueled
explanation: For manually operated drain valves, the driver must drain the tanks at the end of each day of driving.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.4, Air Tank Drains

question: The safety relief valve installed in the first tank the compressor pumps air to is usually set to open at what pressure?
explanation: The safety valve protects the tank and system from too much pressure and is usually set to open at 150 psi.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.6, Safety Valve

question: In an S-cam brake, what happens when air pressure pushes the brake chamber rod out?
choice_a: It directly clamps a disc between friction pads
choice_b: It moves the slack adjuster, twisting the camshaft and turning the S-cam, which forces the brake shoes against the drum
explanation: Air pressure pushes the rod out, moving the slack adjuster and twisting the camshaft, which turns the S-cam and forces the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.8, S-cam Brakes

question: A visible low air pressure warning signal must come on before air pressure in the tanks falls below what level?
explanation: A warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi (or one-half the compressor governor cut-out pressure on older vehicles).
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.11, Low Air Pressure Warning

question: What is a "wig wag" warning device?
choice_a: A buzzer that sounds continuously below 100 psi
choice_b: A mechanical arm that drops into view when pressure drops below 60 psi
choice_c: A dashboard light that flashes when the parking brake is set
choice_d: A gauge needle that turns red at 125 psi
explanation: The wig wag device drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when the pressure in the system drops below 60 psi.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.11, Low Air Pressure Warning

question: According to the manual, what have tests shown about front-wheel skids from braking?
choice_a: They are very likely, even on dry pavement
choice_b: They are not likely, even on ice
explanation: Tests have shown front-wheel skids from braking are not likely, even on ice, so the control should be kept in the normal position for normal stopping power.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.13, Front Brake Limiting Valve

question: Why must emergency and parking brakes on trucks, truck tractors and buses be held on by mechanical force?
choice_a: Because air pressure can eventually leak away
choice_b: Because mechanical force is faster than air pressure
choice_c: Because it is cheaper to manufacture
explanation: Emergency and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force because air pressure can eventually leak away; spring brakes are usually used to meet this need.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.14, Spring Brakes

question: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to what range?
explanation: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.14, Spring Brakes

question: In newer vehicles with air brakes, what does the diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull parking brake control knob do when pulled out?
choice_b: It puts on the parking brakes (spring brakes)
explanation: You pull the knob out to put the parking brakes (spring brakes) on and push it in to release them.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.15, Parking Brake Controls

question: What caution does the manual give regarding pushing the brake pedal down while the spring brakes are on?
choice_a: It is required to release the spring brakes
choice_b: The brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure
choice_c: It has no effect on the brake system
choice_d: It automatically triggers the safety relief valve
explanation: The manual warns never to push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on, because the brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.15, Parking Brake Controls

question: What is the purpose of a modulating control valve on the dashboard?
choice_a: To gradually apply the spring brakes so the driver has a feel for the braking action
choice_b: To automatically drain the air tanks
choice_c: To control the front brake limiting valve
choice_d: To adjust the alcohol evaporator level
explanation: A modulating valve allows a driver to apply the spring brakes gradually; it is spring-loaded so the driver has a feel for the braking action, and lets the driver control spring brakes if the service brakes fail.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.15, Modulating Control Valves

question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date are required to be equipped with antilock brakes (ABS)?
explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.16, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers and converter dollies) built on or after what date are required to have ABS?
explanation: Other air brakes vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.16, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten a vehicle's stopping distance?
choice_a: Yes, it always shortens stopping distance significantly
choice_b: No, but it helps the driver keep the vehicle under control during hard braking
choice_c: Yes, but only on wet pavement
choice_d: No, ABS has no effect on vehicle control
explanation: ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, but it does help the driver keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.1.16, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: In a dual air brake system, what is the system that typically operates the regular brakes on the front axle called?
explanation: One system (the primary system) typically operates the rear axle brakes, while the other (the secondary system) operates the front axle brakes, and possibly one rear axle.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.2, Dual Air Brake

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, the air compressor should be allowed to build up a minimum pressure of how much in both the primary and secondary systems?
explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.2, Dual Air Brake

question: When checking slack adjusters on S-cam brakes, how far can a slack adjuster move at the point where the push rod attaches before it probably needs adjustment?
explanation: If a slack adjuster moves more than about 1 inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.3.2, Check Slack Adjusters on S-cam Brakes

question: What does the manual identify as the most common problem found in roadside inspections?
explanation: The manual states out-of-adjustment brakes are the most common problem found in roadside inspections.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.3.2, Check Slack Adjusters on S-cam Brakes

question: All vehicles built since what year have automatic slack adjusters?
explanation: The manual states all vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjusters.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.3.2, Check Slack Adjusters on S-cam Brakes

question: During the final air brake check, the low air pressure warning signal must come on before the pressure drops below what level in the tank with the lowest air pressure?
explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must come on before the pressure drops to less than 60 psi in the air tank (or tank with the lowest air pressure, in dual air systems).
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.3.3, Test Low Pressure Warning Signal

question: When checking rate of air pressure buildup with the engine at operating rpms in a dual air system, pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within what time?
explanation: In dual air systems, the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds when the engine is at operating rpms.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.3.3, Check Rate of Air Pressure Buildup

question: During the air leakage rate test with the parking brake released and engine off, the loss rate for a single vehicle should be less than what amount in one minute?
explanation: The loss rate should be less than 2 psi in one minute for single vehicles and less than 3 psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.3.3, Test Air Leakage Rate

question: If only the tractor has ABS and the trailer begins to swing out, what should the driver do?
choice_b: Let up on the brakes, if it can be done safely
explanation: When only the tractor has ABS, the driver should keep an eye on the trailer and let up on the brakes (if safe to do so) if it begins to swing out.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.2, Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: What is the one exception in which a driver may fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop according to the manual's ABS guidance?
choice_a: Any time the vehicle is lightly loaded
choice_b: If you always drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles
explanation: The one exception noted is that if you always drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, in an emergency stop you can fully apply the brakes.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.2, Braking with Antilock Brakes

question: In the controlled braking method for emergency stops, how hard should the brakes be applied?
choice_a: As hard as possible, immediately locking the wheels
choice_b: As hard as you can without locking the wheels, with very small steering movements
explanation: With controlled braking, you apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.3, Controlled Braking

question: In the stab braking method, how long can it take for the wheels to start rolling again after the brakes are released?
explanation: It can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after the brakes are released; reapplying before that will prevent the vehicle from straightening out.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.3, Stab Braking

question: What is "brake lag" as it relates to air brakes?
choice_a: The time it takes for the driver to perceive a hazard
choice_b: The time required for the brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed
choice_c: The distance the vehicle travels after coming to a full stop
choice_d: The delay before the parking brake engages
explanation: Brake lag is the time required for the brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed; with air brakes it takes one-half second or more for air to flow through the lines.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.4, Stopping Distance

question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, about how much distance does air brake lag add to the total stopping distance?
explanation: The air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet, making the total stopping distance over 450 feet under good conditions.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.4, Stopping Distance

question: What causes brake fade according to the manual?
choice_a: Excessive heat from overuse, causing chemical changes in the brake lining and expansion of the brake drums
choice_b: Cold weather freezing the brake fluid
explanation: Brake fade results from excessive heat causing chemical changes in the brake lining, which reduce friction, and also causing expansion of the brake drums.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.5, Brake Fading or Failure

question: On a long or steep downgrade, brake use is only a supplement to what?
choice_a: The braking effect of the engine
explanation: The manual states the use of brakes on a long and/or steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine, once the vehicle is in the proper low gear.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.6, Proper Braking Technique

question: On a downgrade, once speed is reduced to approximately 5 mph below the safe speed, how long should the brake application last before releasing?
choice_d: Until the vehicle comes to a complete stop
explanation: When speed is reduced to approximately 5 mph below the safe speed, the brakes are released; this application should last for about three seconds.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.6, Proper Braking Technique

question: Why might a lightly loaded vehicle or a vehicle on slippery roads skid out of control when the spring brakes come on?
choice_a: Because the spring brakes apply full force to all axles equally
choice_b: Because the spring brakes do not work on all axles, and this can cause loss of control especially when lightly loaded or on slippery roads
choice_c: Because the ABS shuts off automatically
choice_d: Because the parking brake control knob sticks
explanation: A heavily loaded vehicle will take a long distance to stop because spring brakes do not work on all axles, while lightly loaded vehicles or vehicles on slippery roads may skid out of control when spring brakes come on.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.7, Low Air Pressure

question: When should a driver avoid using the parking brakes according to the manual?
choice_a: When the vehicle is parked on level ground
choice_b: If the brakes are very hot or very wet in freezing temperatures
choice_c: Whenever the ABS malfunction lamp is on
explanation: Do not use the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot (from a steep grade) or very wet in freezing temperatures, since heat can damage them or freezing can prevent the vehicle from moving.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.8, Parking Brakes

question: What should a driver do if the brakes are wet and cannot be dried before parking on a level surface?
choice_a: Apply the parking brakes as normal
choice_b: Use wheel chocks to hold the vehicle instead, and use the brakes lightly while driving in a low gear to heat and dry them
choice_c: Leave the vehicle unattended with the engine running
choice_d: Disable the low air pressure warning
explanation: Use wheel chocks on a level surface to hold the vehicle if the brakes are hot or wet; if wet, use the brakes lightly while driving in a low gear to heat and dry them.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 5.4.8, Parking Brakes
